exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Code Repositories
exploitedBy.relevance: Anonymous access to code repositories allows unauthenticated users to read sensitive data from information repositories without credentials.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Data from Information Repositories
exploitedBy.relevance: Enabling anonymous access exposes repository data to collection by any unauthenticated actor.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Valid Accounts
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak or missing admin authentication allows adversaries to gain access using valid or easily guessed credentials.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Default Accounts
exploitedBy.relevance: Missing authentication often leaves default admin accounts exploitable by attackers.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credential Stuffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak authentication mechanisms are susceptible to credential stuffing attacks.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Private Keys
exploitedBy.relevance: Exposure of SSH host keys allows adversaries to obtain private keys used for authentication and secure communications.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: SSH Hijacking
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak SSH configuration or key exposure enables session hijacking of existing SSH connections.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: SSH
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak SSH configuration enables attackers to leverage SSH for unauthorized remote access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted HTTP allows interception and exfiltration of data transmitted over plaintext protocols.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Protocol Tunneling
exploitedBy.relevance: Without TLS enforcement, attackers can tunnel malicious traffic through unencrypted HTTP connections.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration to Code Repository
exploitedBy.relevance: Public repository visibility can facilitate unintended data exposure and exfiltration of sensitive source code.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Application Access Token
exploitedBy.relevance: Unrestricted API token issuance allows adversaries to use stolen or generated tokens to authenticate and access resources.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Steal Application Access Token
exploitedBy.relevance: Unrestricted token issuance increases attack surface for stealing application access tokens to impersonate users or services.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Access Token Manipulation
exploitedBy.relevance: Without restrictions on API token issuance, adversaries can manipulate or forge tokens to escalate privileges.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Poisoned Pipeline Execution
exploitedBy.relevance: Unprotected default branches allow adversaries to inject malicious code that executes in CI/CD pipelines.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
exploitedBy.relevance: Unprotected branches enable supply chain compromise by allowing unauthorized modifications to source code and dependencies.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Supply Chain Compromise
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of branch protection allows attackers to tamper with code, compromising the software supply chain.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Webhook
exploitedBy.relevance: Unrestricted webhook targets can be abused to exfiltrate data to attacker-controlled endpoints via SSRF.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Escape to Host
exploitedBy.relevance: A git service running as root or privileged user facilitates container or sandbox escape to the underlying host.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Container Administration Command
exploitedBy.relevance: Privileged process execution enables attackers to run administrative commands within the container environment.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Container Service
exploitedBy.relevance: Running as root allows adversaries to create or modify container services for persistence and privilege escalation.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Data from Cloud Storage
exploitedBy.relevance: Publicly accessible or unencrypted backup storage allows adversaries to directly access and exfiltrate stored backup data.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Disable or Modify Cloud Logs
exploitedBy.relevance: Disabled or incomplete audit logging mirrors the impact of adversaries disabling logs to avoid detection.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Disable Windows Event Logging
exploitedBy.relevance: Incomplete audit logging reduces visibility into attacker activity, analogous to disabling event logging.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Log Enumeration
exploitedBy.relevance: Without complete audit logs, adversaries can enumerate and exploit gaps in logging coverage to evade detection.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
exploitedBy.relevance: Outdated platform versions contain known vulnerabilities that adversaries exploit in public-facing applications.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
exploitedBy.relevance: Unpatched software exposes known vulnerabilities in remote services that attackers can exploit for access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: External Remote Services
exploitedBy.relevance: Network exposure to untrusted segments allows adversaries to access external remote services without proper network controls.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Remote Services
exploitedBy.relevance: Untrusted network access enables adversaries to leverage remote services for lateral movement or initial access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credentials In Files
exploitedBy.relevance: Secrets stored in repository configuration or history represent credentials stored in files that adversaries can discover.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Unsecured Credentials
exploitedBy.relevance: Storing secrets in repository configuration or commit history constitutes unsecured credential storage accessible to attackers.
